summary: This is an Express.js REST API that acts as a wrapper around the ScraperAPI service to scrape Amazon India product data. It provides four endpoints: fetching product details, product reviews, product offers, and search results by passing requests through ScraperAPI with an API key provided by the client.

bugs.description: The ScraperAPI URL in generateScraperUrl is malformed. It uses 'http:api.scarperapi.com' instead of 'http://api.scraperapi.com', and the query parameter separator uses 'api.key=' instead of 'api_key='. This means every request to the scraper will fail.
bugs.suggested_fix: Change the function to: const generateScraperUrl = (apiKey) => `http://api.scraperapi.com?api_key=${apiKey}&autoparse=true`;

bugs.description: The API key is passed as a query parameter (api_key) from the client, which exposes it in server logs, browser history, and HTTP referrer headers. There is no validation that api_key is present or non-empty before using it in requests.
bugs.suggested_fix: Store the API key server-side in an environment variable (process.env.SCRAPER_API_KEY) and never accept it from the client. Add a guard clause to reject requests if the key is missing: if (!process.env.SCRAPER_API_KEY) return res.status(500).json({ error: 'Server misconfiguration' });

bugs.description: User-supplied inputs (productId, searchQuery) are directly interpolated into URLs without any sanitization or encoding. This could allow URL injection attacks or unexpected behavior if special characters are included.
bugs.suggested_fix: Use encodeURIComponent() on user inputs before inserting them into the URL. For example: `&url=https://www.amazon.in/dp/${encodeURIComponent(productId)}`

bugs.description: In the catch blocks, the raw error object is passed directly to res.json(error). Error objects are not always JSON-serializable and may expose sensitive stack traces or internal details to the client.
bugs.suggested_fix: Return a sanitized error response instead: res.status(500).json({ error: error.message || 'An unexpected error occurred' });

bugs.description: JSON.parse(response) is called without a try/catch guard. If the response from ScraperAPI is not valid JSON (e.g., an HTML error page), this will throw an unhandled exception and crash the handler before the catch block for the outer request can cleanly process it.
bugs.suggested_fix: Wrap JSON.parse in its own try/catch, or use a helper function. Alternatively, configure the request library to parse JSON automatically using { json: true } in the options.

bugs.description: The commented-out code at lines 7-8 contains a syntax error in the comment itself ('generateScraperUrl(api_key) =' is not valid JS syntax). While harmless as a comment, it is misleading and should be removed.
bugs.suggested_fix: Remove the commented-out lines 7 and 8 to keep the codebase clean.
